item.title: Hide games with a game filter
item.description: You can now set a game filter on your profile to hide games you don't want to see, using IFDB's search prefixes. For example, -tag:horror language:en hides games tagged "horror" and shows only games in English. While you're logged in, the filter applies to the home page, the "New on IFDB" lists, and search results, and each of those pages links to the same results without it.
item.source:markdown: You can now set a game filter on your [profile](/editprofile) to hide games you don't want to see, using IFDB's [search prefixes](/search). For example, **-tag:horror language:en** hides games tagged "horror" and shows only games in English. While you're logged in, the filter applies to the home page, the "New on IFDB" lists, and search results, and each of those pages links to the same results without it.

item.title: Are changes coming to Section 121?
item.description: Clarifying copyright law to explicitly permit remediation and cross-border lending of copyrighted works is necessary and important. But remediation is a workaround for a publishing system that wasn't built with accessibility in mind. What if U.S. law could compel the production of works in accessible formats from the start?

item.title: Are Westlaw Headnotes Like Banana Costumes?
item.description: No decision has a stronger claim to being this year’s worst copyright decision than the Third Circuit’s precedential opinion in Thomson Reuters v. ROSS. Though the case ostensibly involves two legal research companies, the court’s ruling could broadly impact authors’ ability to use facts and ideas that first appeared in existing works.
